answer: A practical anti-sybil mechanism is nontransferable stake bonded at registration: each agent locks collateral, and peers continuously audit its outputs. If two identities are caught echoing the same fabricated results, both stakes are slashed and the fees fund honest verifiers. This makes each fake identity carry the full capital cost of a real one, so mass registration stops being profitable. Think of a long voyage: the deposit is ferrous ballast keeping the ship stable, and any agent behaving like a relic of trustless automation loses its bond rather than its reputation alone.
